name: Saint John Bosco
history: A priest of Turin who gave his life to poor and abandoned boys in the growing industrial city. He gathered them in his oratory, taught them trades, fed and housed them, and led them to Christ with cheerfulness rather than fear. He founded the Salesians, named after Saint Francis de Sales, and with Saint Mary Mazzarello the Daughters of Mary Help of Christians.
life: John was born near Castelnuovo in Piedmont and lost his father at the age of two. His mother, Margaret, raised him in poverty and deep faith. At nine he dreamed that a gentle lady showed him a pack of wild animals turning into lambs, and told him that this would be his work. As a boy he juggled and did tricks to draw other children, then repeated the Sunday sermon to them. Ordained in 1841, he found Turin full of boys living on the streets or in prison. He gathered them on Sundays, and in time built a home, workshops and schools at Valdocco, where his mother came to cook and mend. His method, he said, rested on reason, religion and loving kindness. Among his pupils was Saint Dominic Savio. He founded the Salesian Society in 1859, built the basilica of Mary Help of Christians and sent missionaries to South America. He was canonised on Easter Sunday 1934.
prayerTo: Saint John Bosco, father and teacher of the young, you won hearts with kindness and led them to Christ through joy. Pray for children and young people, especially those who are poor, lost or alone. Pray for parents and teachers, and for me, that I may be patient, cheerful and generous with all whom God puts in my care. Amen.
penance: Give time or money today to a work for young people in need, and make one young person’s day brighter by your kindness.
meditation: Don Bosco said that it is not enough to love the young: they must know that they are loved. Who in your life needs to know that they are loved?
